units.zh: 郭崇韜，字安時，代州雁門人也。
units.en: Guo Chongtao, whose style name was Anshi, was a native of Yanmen in Dai Prefecture.
units.literal: Guo Chongtao, style Anshi, was a man of Yanmen in Dai Prefecture.

units.zh: 父宏正。
units.en: His father was Hongzheng.
units.literal: His father was Hongzheng.

units.zh: 崇韜初為李克修帳下親信。
units.en: Chongtao began as a trusted confidant in Li Kexiu's personal entourage.
units.literal: At first Chongtao served as a trusted intimate beneath Li Kexiu's command tent.

units.zh: 克修鎮昭義，崇韜累典事務，以廉幹稱。
units.en: While Kexiu held the Zhaoyi command, Chongtao repeatedly handled administrative affairs and earned a reputation for integrity and efficiency.
units.literal: When Kexiu garrisoned Zhaoyi, Chongtao repeatedly managed affairs and was renowned for integrity and competence.

units.zh: 克修卒，武皇用為典謁，奉使鳳翔稱旨，署教練使。
units.en: After Kexiu's death, Emperor Wu appointed him Master of Ceremonies. On an embassy to Fengxiang he fulfilled his mission to the emperor's satisfaction and was made Training Commissioner.
units.literal: When Kexiu died, Emperor Wu employed him as Master of Ceremonies; on a mission to Fengxiang he pleased the intent, and was appointed Training Commissioner.

units.zh: 崇韜臨事機警，應對可觀。
units.en: In handling affairs Chongtao was alert and resourceful, and his replies were impressive.
units.literal: In attending to affairs Chongtao was quick-witted, and his responses were admirable.

units.zh: 莊宗嗣位，尤器重之。
units.en: When Emperor Zhuangzong took the throne, he placed exceptional trust in him.
units.literal: When Zhuangzong succeeded to the throne, he especially valued and trusted him.

units.zh: 天祐十四年，用為中門副使，與孟知祥、李紹宏俱參機要。
units.en: In the fourteenth year of Tianyou he was appointed Vice Commissioner of the Inner Gate and, together with Meng Zhixiang and Li Shaohong, shared in confidential state affairs.
units.literal: In the fourteenth year of Tianyou, he was employed as Vice Commissioner of the Inner Gate, and together with Meng Zhixiang and Li Shaohong all participated in vital secrets.

units.zh: 俄而紹宏出典幽州留事，知祥懇辭要職。
units.en: Soon afterward Shaohong was sent to administer Youzhou as resident commissioner, and Zhixiang earnestly sought to relinquish his key post.
units.literal: Before long Shaohong went out to govern Youzhou as resident commissioner; Zhixiang earnestly declined the vital post.

units.zh: 先是，中門使吳珙、張虔厚忠而獲罪。
units.en: Previously, the Inner Gate commissioners Wu Gong and Zhang Qianhou had been loyal men who nevertheless fell under accusation.
units.literal: Earlier, Inner Gate Commissioners Wu Gong and Zhang Qianhou had been loyal yet incurred guilt.

units.zh: 知祥懼，求為外任，妻矞華公主泣請於貞簡太后。
units.en: Meng Zhixiang grew fearful and petitioned for a provincial assignment; his wife, Princess Yuhua, tearfully appealed to Empress Dowager Zhenjian.
units.literal: Zhixiang feared, and sought an external assignment; his wife Princess Yuhua wept and begged Empress Dowager Zhenjian.

units.zh: 莊宗謂知祥曰：「公欲避路，當舉其代。」
units.en: Emperor Zhuangzong said to Meng Zhixiang, "If you wish to step aside, you must name your successor."
units.literal: Zhuangzong said to Zhixiang: "If you, sir, wish to yield the way, you ought to recommend your replacement."

units.zh: 知祥因舉崇韜。
units.en: Zhixiang thereupon nominated Guo Chongtao.
units.literal: Zhixiang thereupon recommended Chongtao.

units.zh: 乃署知祥為太原軍在城都虞候。
units.en: The emperor then appointed Meng Zhixiang Chief Garrison Officer of the Taiyuan army stationed in the capital.
units.literal: Thereupon he appointed Zhixiang Chief Garrison Officer of the Taiyuan Army within the city.

units.zh: 自是崇韜專典機務，艱難戰伐，靡所不從。
units.en: From then on Guo Chongtao alone directed state affairs, accompanying the emperor through every hardship and campaign.
units.literal: From this Chongtao alone managed vital affairs; in hardship and warfare, nothing did he not follow.

units.zh: 十八年，從征張文禮於鎮州。
units.en: In the eighteenth year he accompanied the campaign against Zhang Wenli at Zhen Prefecture.
units.literal: In the eighteenth year, he followed on campaign against Zhang Wenli at Zhenzhou.

units.zh: 契丹引眾至新樂，王師大恐，諸將鹹請退還魏州，莊宗猶豫未決。
units.en: When the Khitans marched on Xinle, the imperial forces were gripped with fear. The generals unanimously urged a retreat to Weizhou, but Emperor Zhuangzong remained undecided.
units.literal: The Khitans led their masses to Xinle; the imperial army was greatly afraid; the various generals all petitioned to withdraw back to Weizhou; Zhuangzong hesitated and had not decided.

units.zh: 崇韜曰：「阿保機隻為王都所誘，本利貨財，非敦鄰好，苟前鋒小衄，遁走必矣。
units.en: Guo Chongtao said, "Abaoji was lured here by Wang Du alone. He came for loot, not out of genuine alliance. If our vanguard inflicts even a minor defeat, he is certain to flee.
units.literal: Chongtao said: "Abaoji came only because Wang Du enticed him; he originally sought profit in goods and wealth, not sincere neighborly goodwill. If the vanguard suffers a small setback, he will surely flee away.

units.zh: 況我新破汴寇，威振北地，乘此驅攘，焉往不捷！
units.en: And we have just crushed the Liang forces and now dominate the north. If we press this advantage, where can we fail to prevail?
units.literal: Moreover we have newly broken the Bian bandits; our authority shakes the northern lands. Riding this to drive and scatter them—where would we go and not be victorious!

units.zh: 且事之濟否，亦有天命。」
units.en: Besides, whether we succeed also rests with Heaven's mandate."
units.literal: Moreover whether affairs succeed or not also has the Mandate of Heaven."

units.zh: 莊宗從之，王師果捷。
units.en: The emperor took his advice, and the imperial army duly won the day.
units.literal: Zhuangzong followed this; the imperial army indeed was victorious.

units.zh: 明年，李存審收鎮州，遣崇韜閱其府庫，或以珍貨賂遺，一無所取，但市書籍而已。
units.en: The following year, after Li Cunshen recovered Zhen Prefecture, he sent Guo Chongtao to inspect its treasury. Many offered him precious gifts, but he accepted nothing and bought only books.
units.literal: The next year, Li Cunshen recovered Zhenzhou and dispatched Chongtao to inspect its treasury stores. Some tried to bribe him with precious goods; he took not one thing, but only purchased books.

units.zh: 莊宗即位於魏州，崇韜加檢校太保、守兵部尚書，充樞密使。
units.en: When Emperor Zhuangzong took the throne at Weizhou, Guo Chongtao was promoted to Honorary Grand Mentor and Acting Minister of War and appointed Chief Privy Commissioner.
units.literal: When Zhuangzong ascended the throne at Weizhou, Chongtao was additionally made Honorary Grand Mentor, Acting Minister of War, and appointed Chief Privy Commissioner.

units.zh: 是時，衛州陷於梁，澶、相之間，寇鈔日至，民流地削，軍儲不給，群情恟恟，以為霸業終不能就，崇韜寢不安席。
units.en: At that time Weizhou had fallen to Liang, and between Chan and Xiang raids occurred daily. The people fled, territory shrank, and military supplies ran short. Morale collapsed as many concluded the quest for empire was doomed, and Guo Chongtao could not rest easy.
units.literal: At this time Weizhou had fallen to Liang; between Chan and Xiang, bandit raids came daily; the people fled and territory shrank; military stores were insufficient; public sentiment was alarmed, thinking the hegemonic enterprise would never be achieved; Chongtao could not sleep peacefully on his mat.

units.zh: 俄而王彥章陷德勝南城，敵勢滋蔓，汴人急攻楊劉城。
units.en: Soon Wang Yanzhang captured the southern sector of Desheng, enemy strength swelled, and the Liang forces pressed hard against Yangliu.
units.literal: Before long Wang Yanzhang captured the southern city of Desheng; the enemy's momentum spread; the men of Bian urgently attacked Yangliu city.

units.zh: 明宗在鄆，音驛斷絕。
units.en: Emperor Mingzong was at Yun, and all lines of communication had been severed.
units.literal: Mingzong was at Yun; messages and post stations were cut off.

units.zh: 莊宗登城四望，計無所出。
units.en: Emperor Zhuangzong climbed the city wall and scanned the horizon, but no plan suggested itself.
units.literal: Zhuangzong ascended the wall and looked in the four directions; no plan could be devised.

units.zh: 崇韜啟曰：「段凝阻絕津路，苟王師不南，鄆州安能保守！
units.en: Guo Chongtao addressed him, saying, "Duan Ning has cut the river crossings. If our army does not advance south, how can Yun be held?
units.literal: Chongtao submitted, saying: "Duan Ning has blocked and cut off the ford routes. If the imperial army does not go south, how can Yun Prefecture be kept and defended!

units.zh: 臣請於博州東岸立柵，以固通津，但慮汴人偵知，徑來薄我，請陛下募敢死之士，日以挑戰，如三四日間。
units.en: I propose building fortifications on the east bank of the Bo River to secure the crossing, but I fear the Liang may learn of it and strike at us directly. Your Majesty should recruit fearless soldiers to engage them in daily skirmishes—for three or four days.
units.literal: Your subject requests to erect palisades on the east bank of Bozhou to secure the passage ford; but I fear the men of Bian will spy and learn of it and come straight to press upon us. I request Your Majesty recruit dare-to-die warriors and daily provoke battle—for about three or four days.

units.zh: 賊軍未至，則柵壘成矣。」
units.en: Before the enemy reaches us, the fortifications will be finished."
units.literal: Before the bandit army arrives, the palisade fortifications will be completed."

units.zh: 崇韜率毛璋等萬人夜趨博州，視矛戟之端有光，崇韜曰：「吾聞火出兵刃，破賊之兆也。」
units.en: Guo Chongtao led Mao Zhang and ten thousand men on a forced night march to Bozhou. When he saw light gleaming on spear and halberd points, he said, "I have heard that fire on weapons portends victory over the enemy."
units.literal: Chongtao led Mao Zhang and others, ten thousand men, rushing by night to Bozhou. Seeing the tips of spears and halberds had light, Chongtao said: "I have heard fire issuing from weapons is an omen of breaking the bandits."

units.zh: 至博州，渡河版築，晝夜不息。
units.en: Reaching Bozhou, they crossed the river and threw up earthworks without pause day or night.
units.literal: Arriving at Bozhou, they crossed the river and built ramparts, day and night without ceasing.

units.zh: 崇韜於葭葦間據胡床假寢，覺褲中冷，左右視之，乃蛇也，其忘疲勵力也如是。
units.en: Once, while resting on a camp stool among the reeds, Guo Chongtao felt something cold in his trousers; his attendants looked and found a snake. Such was his oblivious devotion to the work.
units.literal: Chongtao among the reeds sat on a folding stool feigning sleep; feeling cold in his trousers, those beside him looked—it was a snake. His forgetting fatigue and exerting effort was like this.

units.zh: 居三日，梁軍果至，城壘低庳，沙土散惡，戰具不完，汴將王彥章、杜晏球率眾攻擊，軍不得休息。
units.en: Three days later the Liang army arrived. The walls were low, the soil loose and poor, and the equipment incomplete. Wang Yanzhang and Du Yanqiu of Liang led their forces in repeated assaults, giving the defenders no respite.
units.literal: After three days, the Liang army indeed arrived. The city fortifications were low and small; sand and earth were loose and poor; battle equipment was incomplete. The Bian generals Wang Yanzhang and Du Yanqiu led the masses in attack; the army could not rest.

units.zh: 崇韜身先督眾，四面拒戰，有急即應，城垂陷，俄報莊宗領親軍次西岸，梁軍聞之退走，因解楊劉之圍。
units.en: Guo Chongtao personally directed the defense on every side, rushing wherever the fighting was fiercest. The city was near capture when word came that Emperor Zhuangzong had reached the west bank with his elite guard. The Liang army withdrew at the news, lifting the siege of Yangliu.
units.literal: Chongtao personally took the lead supervising the masses, resisting battle on four sides; wherever there was urgency he responded. The city was on the verge of falling; soon it was reported that Zhuangzong led the personal army encamped on the west bank; the Liang army heard this and withdrew and fled, thereby relieving the siege of Yangliu.

units.zh: 未幾，汴將康延孝來奔，崇韜延於臥內，訊其軍機。
units.en: Soon afterward the Liang general Kang Yanxiao defected to them. Guo Chongtao received him in his quarters and questioned him about enemy dispositions.
units.literal: Before long the Bian general Kang Yanxiao came to defect; Chongtao received him in his private chamber and interrogated him on military secrets.

units.zh: 延孝曰：「汴人將四道齊舉，以困我軍。」
units.en: Kang Yanxiao said, "The Liang intend a four-pronged advance to pin down our forces."
units.literal: Yanxiao said: "The men of Bian will together raise four routes to hem in our army."

units.zh: 莊宗憂之，召諸將謀進取之策。
units.en: The emperor was deeply troubled and summoned his generals to devise an offensive strategy.
units.literal: Zhuangzong worried over this and summoned the various generals to plan strategies for advance and seizure.

units.zh: 宣徽使李紹宏請棄鄆州，與汴人盟，以河為界，無相侵寇。
units.en: Chief Palace Attendant Li Shaohong proposed abandoning Yun, concluding a treaty with Liang with the Yellow River as the border and a mutual pledge against raiding.
units.literal: Chief Palace Attendant Li Shaohong petitioned to abandon Yun Prefecture, ally with the men of Bian with the river as boundary, and have no mutual invasion or raid.

units.zh: 莊宗不悅，獨臥帳中，召崇韜謂曰：「計將安出？」
units.en: Emperor Zhuangzong was displeased. Retiring alone to his tent, he summoned Guo Chongtao and asked, "What is your plan?"
units.literal: Zhuangzong was displeased; alone he lay in his tent and summoned Chongtao, saying: "What plan shall go forth?"

units.zh: 對曰：「臣不知書，不能征比前古，請以時事言之。
units.en: He answered, "I am no scholar and cannot marshal precedents from antiquity, so let me speak from present circumstances alone.
units.literal: He replied, saying: "Your subject does not know books and cannot cite and compare with former antiquity. I ask to speak according to present affairs.

units.zh: 自陛下十五年起義圖霸，為雪家讎國恥，甲胄生蟣虱，黎人困輸挽。
units.en: Since Your Majesty took up arms at fifteen to forge an empire and avenge your family's wrongs and the nation's shame, armor has rusted on men's backs and the people have been broken by conscription and supply levies.
units.literal: From when Your Majesty at age fifteen raised righteous arms to plot hegemony, to avenge family feud and national shame—armor and helmets bred lice; the common people were exhausted in transport and hauling.

units.zh: 今纂崇大號，河朔士庶，日望蕩平，才得汶陽尺寸之地，不敢保守，況盡有中原乎！
units.en: You have now ascended the throne, and the people of the north look daily for final victory. Yet having gained only a foothold in Wenyang, would you dare not hold it—let alone quit the field when all the Central Plain lies within reach?
units.literal: Now having received the exalted title, the scholars and commoners of Heshuo daily look to complete pacification. Having just obtained a measure of land in Wenyang, you dare not keep and defend it—how much less possessing all the Central Plain!

units.zh: 將來歲賦不充，物議谘怨，設若劃河為界，誰為陛下守之？
units.en: Annual revenue will fail, public resentment will swell, and if we carve out the river as a border, who will defend it for you?
units.literal: In the future yearly revenue will not be sufficient; public talk will murmur and blame. If we demarcate the river as boundary, who will guard it for Your Majesty?

units.zh: 臣自延孝言事以來，晝夜籌度，料我兵力，算賊事機，不出今年，雌雄必決。
units.en: Since Kang Yanxiao's report I have reckoned day and night on our strength and the enemy's design. Victory or defeat must be decided this year.
units.literal: Your subject, from the time Yanxiao spoke of affairs, day and night has calculated and measured, assessed our military strength, reckoned the bandits' strategic opportunities—I reckon that within this year, victory and defeat must be decided.

units.zh: 聞汴人決河，自滑至鄆，非舟楫不能濟。
units.en: I have learned that the Liang have diverted the river from Hua to Yun, so crossing south requires boats.
units.literal: I hear the men of Bian have breached the river from Hua to Yun; without boats and oars one cannot cross.

units.zh: 又聞精兵盡在段凝麾下，王彥章日寇鄆境，彼既以大軍臨我南鄙，又憑恃決河，謂我不能南渡，志在收復汶陽，此汴人之謀也。
units.en: Their best troops are massed under Duan Ning, while Wang Yanzhang harasses Yun daily. They mean to pin us with a great army on our southern frontier while trusting the breached river to keep us from crossing south and reconquering Wenyang. That is the Liang plan.
units.literal: I also hear that elite troops are all under Duan Ning's command; Wang Yanzhang daily raids the Yun border. They both with a great army press our southern frontier and rely on the breached river, thinking we cannot cross south—their aim is to recover Wenyang. This is the Bian people's stratagem.

units.zh: 臣謂段凝保據河壖，苟欲持我，臣但請留兵守鄴，保固楊劉；
units.en: Leave Duan Ning to hold the river line while he tries to pin us down. Leave enough troops to hold Ye and secure Yangliu;
units.literal: Your subject believes Duan Ning holds and occupies the river embankments, merely wishing to contain us. Your subject only asks to leave troops to guard Ye and securely defend Yangliu;

units.zh: 陛下親禦六軍，長驅倍道，直指大梁，汴城無兵，望風自潰。
units.en: Your Majesty should lead the main army in forced march straight upon Daliang. Bianliang stands undefended and will crumble at your approach.
units.literal: Your Majesty personally leads the Six Armies, driving long at double speed, pointing straight at Daliang; Bian city has no troops and will collapse at the wind of your approach.

units.zh: 若使偽主授首，賊將自然倒戈，半月之間，天下必定。
units.en: Once their pretender is captured, their generals will defect of their own accord, and within half a month the realm will be settled.
units.literal: If we cause the false lord to surrender his head, the bandit generals will naturally turn their blades; within half a month, all under Heaven will surely be settled.

units.zh: 如不決此計，傍采浮譚，臣恐不能濟也。
units.en: If you do not commit to this plan and instead heed every idle rumor, I fear we will achieve nothing.
units.literal: If Your Majesty does not resolve upon this plan but instead heeds idle gossip on the side, I fear success will be impossible.

units.zh: 今歲秋稼不登，軍糧才支數月，決則成敗未知，不決則坐見不濟。
units.en: The autumn harvest has failed this year, and our military stores will last only a few months. To act is to gamble on an uncertain outcome; to hesitate is to watch defeat arrive without lifting a hand.
units.literal: This year's autumn harvest has failed; army provisions will last only a few months. To decide is to gamble on an unknown outcome; not to decide is to sit and watch failure come.

units.zh: 臣聞作舍道邊，三年不成，帝王應運，必有天命，成敗天也，在陛下獨斷。」
units.en: They say a house built by the roadside never gets finished in three years, yet an emperor who rises by Heaven's decree cannot lack Heaven's mandate. Victory or defeat is Heaven's to grant—it is for Your Majesty alone to decide."
units.literal: I have heard that building a house beside the road takes three years without completion, yet an emperor who rises by Heaven's favor must have Heaven's mandate. Success or failure lies with Heaven—it rests with Your Majesty alone to decide."

units.zh: 莊宗蹶然而興曰：「正合吾意。
units.en: Zhuangzong leapt to his feet and declared, "That is precisely what I mean.
units.literal: Emperor Zhuangzong suddenly rose and said: "That is exactly my intention.

units.zh: 丈夫得則為王，失則為擄，行計決矣！」
units.en: Win and you are king; lose and you are a prisoner—the course is set!"
units.literal: A man who succeeds becomes king; who fails becomes a captive—the plan is settled!"

units.zh: 即日下令軍中，家口並還魏州。
units.en: That same day he ordered the army to send all dependents back to Weizhou.
units.literal: That same day he issued orders throughout the army: all dependents were to return to Weizhou.

units.zh: 莊宗送劉皇后與興聖宮使繼岌至朝城西野亭泣別，曰：「事勢危蹙，今須一決，事苟不濟，無復相見。」
units.en: Zhuangzong saw Empress Liu and Jiji, Director of the Palace of Exalted Sanctity, off to the wild pavilion west of Chaocheng, weeping as he parted from them. He said, "The crisis leaves no room for delay—we must settle this now. If we fail, we will never see each other again."
units.literal: Emperor Zhuangzong escorted Empress Liu and Director of the Palace of Exalted Sanctity Jiji to the wild pavilion west of Chaocheng and parted from them in tears, saying: "The situation is perilously tight; we must settle this once and for all. If matters fail, we shall never meet again."

units.zh: 乃留李紹宏及租庸使張憲守魏州，大軍自楊劉濟河。
units.en: He left Li Shaohong and Zhang Xian, Commissioner of Land Tax, to hold Weizhou, while the main force crossed the river from Yangliu.
units.literal: He then left Li Shaohong and Commissioner of Land Tax Zhang Xian to defend Weizhou, while the main army crossed the river from Yangliu.

units.zh: 是歲，擒王彥章，誅梁氏，降段凝，皆崇韜讚成其謀也。
units.en: That year Wang Yanzhang was captured, the Liang dynasty was overthrown, and Duan Ning surrendered—all achievements that Guo Chongtao had urged and helped bring to pass.
units.literal: That year Wang Yanzhang was captured, the Liang house was destroyed, and Duan Ning surrendered—all through Guo Chongtao's counsel in bringing the plan to fruition.

units.zh: 莊宗至汴州，宰相豆盧革在魏州，令崇韜權行中書事。
units.en: When Zhuangzong arrived at Bianzhou, Grand Counselor Doulu Ge remained at Weizhou, and Zhuangzong put Guo Chongtao in charge of Secretariat affairs on a provisional basis.
units.literal: When Emperor Zhuangzong reached Bianzhou, Grand Counselor Doulu Ge was at Weizhou, so he had Guo Chongtao act provisionally as chief of the Secretariat.

units.zh: 俄拜侍中兼樞密使，及郊禮畢，以崇韜兼領鎮、冀州節度使，進封趙郡公，邑二千戶，賜鐵券，恕十死。
units.en: He was soon made Palace Attendant while retaining his post as Commissioner of Military Affairs. After the suburban rites, Guo Chongtao was also appointed military governor of Zhen and Ji, ennobled as Duke of Zhao with a fief of two thousand households, and granted an iron certificate absolving him of ten capital offenses.
units.literal: Soon he was appointed Palace Attendant concurrently as Commissioner of Military Affairs; after the suburban sacrifices were completed, Guo Chongtao was also made military governor of Zhen and Ji prefectures, advanced to Duke of Zhao Commandery with a fief of two thousand households, and granted an iron certificate forgiving ten deaths.

units.zh: 崇韜既位極人臣，權傾內外，謀猷獻納，必盡忠規，士族朝倫，頗亦收獎人物，內外翕然稱之。
units.en: With Guo Chongtao at the summit of power, his influence extending throughout court and realm, every proposal he submitted was forthright loyal counsel. He also patronized and promoted talented men among the gentry and court officials, and acclaim for him was widespread within and without.
units.literal: Now that Guo Chongtao had reached the apex of official rank and his power swayed court and realm alike, every plan he offered was fully loyal counsel. Among the gentry and court officials he also recruited and rewarded talent, and inside and out all joined in praising him.

units.zh: 初收汴、洛，稍通賂遺，親友或規之，崇韜曰：「餘備位將相，祿賜巨萬，但偽梁之日，賂遺成風，今方面藩侯，多梁之舊將，皆吾君射鉤斬祛之人也。
units.en: After the capture of Bian and Luoyang, he allowed some exchange of gifts and bribes. When friends and relatives counseled him against it, Guo Chongtao said, "I occupy the rank of general and minister, with emoluments in the tens of thousands. Yet under the false Liang, bribery was endemic; most of the frontier lords today are former Liang commanders—men our lord once had reason to kill but chose to spare.
units.literal: When Bian and Luoyang were first taken, gifts and bribes flowed freely. Friends and kin sometimes admonished him. Guo Chongtao said: "I hold the rank of general and minister, with salary and gifts in the tens of thousands. But in the days of the false Liang, bribery was the custom; today the regional lords are mostly former Liang generals—men whom our lord once marked with an arrow at the belt and cut the sleeve to spare.

units.zh: 一旦革麵，化為吾人，堅拒其請，得無懼乎！
units.en: They have changed sides overnight and become our allies—if I refuse their gifts outright, will they not take alarm!
units.literal: Once they change their allegiance overnight and become our men, if I steadfastly refuse their requests, will they not take alarm!

units.zh: 藏餘私室，無異公帑。」
units.en: Whatever I receive goes into my private store—but it is no different from the public purse."
units.literal: What I store in my private quarters is no different from the public treasury."

units.zh: 及郊禋，崇韜悉獻家財，以助賞給。
units.en: At the suburban sacrifice, he donated his entire personal fortune to help fund imperial rewards.
units.literal: When the suburban sacrifice came, Guo Chongtao donated his entire family wealth to assist in rewards and grants.

units.zh: 時近臣勸莊宗以貢奉物為內庫，珍貨山積，公府賞軍不足。
units.en: At the time, close advisers urged Zhuangzong to hoard tribute goods in the inner treasury. Precious valuables piled up like mountains, yet the public coffers could not cover military rewards.
units.literal: At that time close attendants urged Zhuangzong to keep tribute goods in the inner treasury; precious goods piled like mountains, while the public office lacked funds to reward the army.

units.zh: 崇韜奏請出內庫之財以助，莊宗沉吟有靳惜之意。
units.en: Guo Chongtao petitioned to draw on the inner treasury to make up the shortfall, but Zhuangzong hesitated, clearly unwilling to spend it.
units.literal: Guo Chongtao memorialized requesting disbursement from the inner treasury to assist; Zhuangzong hesitated, showing reluctance to part with it.

units.zh: 是時天下已定，寇仇外息，莊宗漸務華侈，以逞己欲。
units.en: By then the empire was pacified and external threats had subsided. Zhuangzong gradually gave himself over to luxury and indulgence.
units.literal: By then the realm was settled and external enemies quelled; Zhuangzong gradually turned to lavish display to indulge his desires.

units.zh: 洛陽大內宏敞，宮宇深邃，宦官阿意順旨，以希恩寵，聲言宮中夜見鬼物，不謀同辭。
units.en: The inner palace at Luoyang was vast, its halls deep and sprawling. Eunuchs curried favor by echoing one another's claim that ghostly apparitions were seen in the palace at night.
units.literal: Luoyang's inner palace was vast and spacious, its halls deep and remote. Eunuchs flattered to win favor, claiming in unison that ghostly apparitions were seen in the palace at night.

units.zh: 莊宗駭異其事，且問其故。
units.en: Zhuangzong was disturbed and asked why this should be.
units.literal: Zhuangzong was alarmed and astonished by this and asked the reason.

units.zh: 宦者曰：「見本朝長安大內，六宮嬪御，殆及萬人，椒房蘭室，無不充刃。
units.en: The eunuchs said, "In our dynasty's Chang'an, the inner palace housed nearly ten thousand consorts and concubines from the six palaces. Every chamber was fully occupied.
units.literal: The eunuchs said: "In our dynasty's Chang'an inner palace, the consorts and imperial concubines of the six palaces numbered nearly ten thousand; every orchid chamber and peppered room was filled to the brim.

units.zh: 今宮室大半空閑，鬼神尚幽，亦無所怪。」
units.en: Now most of the palace stands empty. Spirits naturally haunt deserted places—there is nothing surprising in that."
units.literal: Now the palace halls are largely empty and idle; spirits prefer darkness—there is nothing strange in this."

units.zh: 由是景進、王允平等於諸道采擇宮人，不擇良賤，內之宮掖。
units.en: As a result, Jing Jin, Wang Yunping, and others scoured the provinces for palace women, accepting anyone regardless of quality or background, and brought them into the inner quarters.
units.literal: Thereupon Jing Jin, Wang Yunping, and others selected palace women from all circuits, taking them without regard to quality or station, and installed them in the inner palace.

units.zh: 三年夏，雨，河大水，壞天津橋。
units.en: In the third year, summer brought heavy rains; the Yellow River rose in flood and destroyed the Tianjin Bridge.
units.literal: In the third year, summer: rain fell, the Yellow River swelled, and the Tianjin Bridge was destroyed.

units.zh: 是時，酷暑尤甚。
units.en: The heat that summer was exceptionally severe.
units.literal: At that time the heat of summer was especially intense.

units.zh: 莊宗常擇高樓避暑，皆不稱旨。
units.en: Zhuangzong tried one high pavilion after another seeking relief from the heat, but none satisfied him.
units.literal: Zhuangzong often chose tall buildings to escape the heat, but none pleased him.

units.zh: 宦官曰：「今大內樓觀，不及舊時長安卿相之家，舊日大明、興慶兩宮，樓觀百數，皆雕楹畫栱，幹雲蔽日，今官家納涼無可禦者。」
units.en: The eunuchs said, "The towers and halls of today's inner palace cannot compare even with the mansions of Chang'an officials in the old days. The Daming and Xingqing palaces once had hundreds of towers, all with carved pillars and painted brackets soaring to the clouds and blotting out the sun. His Majesty now has nowhere fit to escape the heat."
units.literal: The eunuchs said: "Today's inner palace towers and pavilions do not match even the homes of Chang'an ministers of old. In former days the Daming and Xingqing palaces had towers and halls by the hundreds, all with carved pillars and painted brackets, reaching the clouds and blocking the sun. Today His Majesty has nowhere adequate to escape the heat."

units.zh: 莊宗曰：「餘富有天下，豈不能辦一樓！」
units.en: Zhuangzong replied, "I rule all under Heaven—surely I can afford one tower!"
units.literal: Zhuangzong said: "I possess all under Heaven—can I not build a single tower!"

units.zh: 即令宮苑使經營之，猶慮崇韜有所諫止，使謂崇韜曰：「今年惡熱，朕頃在河上，五六月中，與賊對壘，行宮卑濕，介馬戰賊，恒若清涼。
units.en: He immediately ordered the Director of Palace Parks to begin construction. Still concerned that Guo Chongtao might object, he had someone say to him, "The heat this year is unbearable. When I was on the Yellow River recently, fighting the enemy through the fifth and sixth months from a damp, low camp, riding into battle in armor always felt refreshingly cool.
units.literal: He immediately ordered the Director of Palace Parks to undertake the project. Still fearing Guo Chongtao might remonstrate and stop it, he had someone tell Guo Chongtao: "This year's heat is terrible. When I was recently on the Yellow River, in the fifth and sixth months facing the enemy in camp, the traveling palace was low and damp, yet riding out in armor to fight the enemy, it always felt cool.

units.zh: 今晏然深宮，不耐暑毒，何也？」
units.en: Now I sit at ease in the inner palace and cannot endure the heat—why should that be?"
units.literal: Now I dwell at ease in the deep palace and cannot bear the summer's oppression—why is this?"

units.zh: 崇韜奏：「陛下頃在河上，汴寇未平，廢寢忘食，心在戰陣，祁寒溽暑，不介聖懷。
units.en: Guo Chongtao replied, "When Your Majesty was on the river, the rebels of Bian had not yet been crushed. You went without sleep and food, your mind wholly on the battlefield. Bitter cold and crushing heat alike never touched you.
units.literal: Guo Chongtao memorialized: "When Your Majesty was recently on the river, the Bian rebels were not yet pacified. You neglected sleep and forgot food; your heart was on the battlefield. Extreme cold and sweltering heat alike did not touch Your Majesty's mind.

units.zh: 今寇既平，中原無事，縱耳目之玩，不憂戰陣，雖層台百尺，廣殿九筵，未能忘熱於今日也。
units.en: Now the enemy is defeated and the heartland is at peace. Your mind turns to pleasure and no longer to war—even towers a hundred feet tall and halls nine bays wide cannot make today's heat feel any less.
units.literal: Now the rebels are pacified and the Central Plains are at peace. You indulge sights and sounds and worry no longer about battle. Though you had towers a hundred feet high and halls spanning nine bays, you could not today forget the heat.

units.zh: 願陛下思艱難創業之際，則今日之暑，坐變清涼。」
units.en: If Your Majesty would only remember the hardships of building this empire, today's heat would feel cool enough while you sit still."
units.literal: I pray Your Majesty will recall the hardships of founding the enterprise—then today's heat will turn cool while you sit."

units.zh: 莊宗默然。
units.en: Zhuangzong said nothing.
units.literal: Zhuangzong fell silent.

units.zh: 王允平等竟加營造，崇韜復奏曰：「內中營造，日有縻費，屬當災饉，且乞權停。」
units.en: Wang Yunping and his cohort went on building regardless. Guo Chongtao submitted another memorial: "Palace construction drains resources daily. With famine upon us, I beg that it be suspended for now."
units.literal: Wang Yunping and the others pressed ahead with construction regardless. Guo Chongtao memorialized again: "Construction within the palace daily incurs wasteful expense. We are in the midst of famine—I beg that work be temporarily halted."

units.zh: 不聽。
units.en: The emperor refused to listen.
units.literal: His plea was not heeded.

units.zh: 初，崇韜與李紹宏同為內職，及莊宗即位，崇韜以紹宏素在己上，舊人難製，即奏澤潞監軍張居翰同掌樞密，以紹宏為宣徽使。
units.en: Earlier, Guo Chongtao and Li Shaohong had both served in the inner administration. After Zhuangzong's accession, Guo Chongtao—finding that Li Shaohong had always outranked him and that an old associate was difficult to manage—petitioned to have Zhang Juhán, military commissioner of Ze and Lu, share control of Military Affairs, while appointing Li Shaohong Commissioner of the Palace Secretariat.
units.literal: Initially Guo Chongtao and Li Shaohong both held inner-court posts. When Zhuangzong took the throne, Guo Chongtao, because Li Shaohong had long ranked above him and old colleagues were hard to control, memorialized to have Zhang Juhán, military overseer of Ze and Lu, share charge of Military Affairs, and made Li Shaohong Commissioner of the Palace Secretariat.

units.zh: 紹宏大失所望，泣涕憤鬱。
units.en: Li Shaohong was bitterly disappointed and wept in frustration.
units.literal: Li Shaohong was deeply disappointed; he wept and sank into bitter dejection.

units.zh: 崇韜乃置內勾使，應三司財賦，皆令勾覆，令紹宏領之，冀塞其心。
units.en: Guo Chongtao then created the post of inner auditing commissioner, putting all revenues of the three fiscal bureaus under audit and assigning Li Shaohong to head it, hoping to mollify him.
units.literal: Guo Chongtao then established the post of inner auditor: all revenues and levies of the three bureaus were assigned for audit and verification, with Li Shaohong placed in charge, hoping to placate him.

units.zh: 紹宏怏悵不已。
units.en: Li Shaohong remained aggrieved and unsatisfied.
units.literal: Li Shaohong remained resentful and discontented.

units.zh: 崇韜自以有大功，河、洛平定之後，權位熏灼，恐為人所傾奪，乃謂諸子曰：「吾佐主上，大事了矣，今為群邪排毀，吾欲避之，歸鎮常山，為菟裘之計。」
units.en: Believing his achievements unrivaled, Guo Chongtao after the pacification of the river lands and Luoyang wielded power so conspicuously that he feared rivals would bring him down. He told his sons, "I have served the emperor well and the great work is finished. Now the wicked circle against me. I mean to withdraw to my post at Changshan and seek a quiet place to live out my days."
units.literal: Guo Chongtao, considering his great merit, after the pacification of the Yellow River region and Luoyang found his power and rank blazing bright and feared others would topple and seize his position. He told his sons: "I have assisted the sovereign; the great task is done. Now I am slandered and driven out by a crowd of villains. I wish to withdraw, return to my command at Changshan, and plan a place of retirement."

units.zh: 其子廷說等曰：「大人功名及此，一失其勢，便是神龍去水，為螻蟻所製，尤宜深察。」
units.en: His sons Tingshuo and the others replied, "Father, you have risen to the height of power. Lose that position and you are a dragon out of water—at the mercy of ants. You must think carefully about this."
units.literal: His sons Tingshuo and others said: "Father, your merit and fame have reached this height. Once you lose that power, it is like a divine dragon leaving the water—you will be controlled by ants. You must consider this deeply."

units.zh: 門人故吏又謂崇韜曰：「侍中勳業第一，雖群官側目，必未能離間。
units.en: His retainers and former subordinates also counseled him: "Your merit is without peer. Though rivals watch you with envy, none can yet come between you and the emperor.
units.literal: His disciples and former subordinates also told Guo Chongtao: "Your Excellency's achievements rank first. Though officials eye you with envy, they surely cannot drive a wedge between you and the throne.

units.zh: 宜於此時堅辭機務，上必不聽，是有辭避之名，塞其讒慝之口。
units.en: You should resign your core duties now. The emperor will refuse, of course—but that gives you the reputation of one who sought to step aside, and it silences the slanderers.
units.literal: You should at this time firmly decline your duties at the center of power. The emperor will surely not agree—that earns you the name of one who withdraws with good reason and shuts the mouths of slanderers.

units.zh: 魏國夫人劉氏有寵，中宮未正，宜讚成冊禮，上心必悅。
units.en: Lady Liu of Wei enjoys the emperor's favor while the empress's throne remains vacant. Urge her formal investiture—the emperor will be delighted.
units.literal: Lady Liu of Wei State enjoys favor and the empress's seat is unfilled; you should urge her enthronement. The emperor's heart will surely be pleased.

units.zh: 內得劉氏之助，群閹其如餘何！」
units.en: With Lady Liu's support within the palace, what can those eunuchs do to you!"
units.literal: With Lady Liu's support within, what can the pack of eunuchs do to me!"

units.zh: 崇韜然之，於是三上章堅辭樞密之位，優詔不從。
units.en: Guo Chongtao took this advice. He submitted three memorials firmly resigning his post as Commissioner of Military Affairs, but each gracious edict from the throne refused his request.
units.literal: Guo Chongtao agreed. Thereupon he thrice submitted memorials firmly declining the post of Commissioner of Military Affairs; gracious edicts refused his requests.

units.zh: 崇韜乃密奏請立魏國夫人為皇后，復奏時務利害二十五條，皆便於時，取悅人心；
units.en: Guo Chongtao then secretly petitioned to have Lady Liu of Wei ennobled as empress. He also submitted twenty-five recommendations on pressing affairs of state—all timely, practical, and designed to win popular approval;
units.literal: Guo Chongtao then secretly memorialized requesting that Lady Liu of Wei State be made empress. He also submitted twenty-five items on the advantages and harms of current affairs—all timely and calculated to win people's hearts;

units.zh: 又請罷樞密院事，各歸本司，以輕其權，然宦官造謗不已。
units.en: He further petitioned to abolish the Bureau of Military Affairs and restore its functions to the regular ministries, thereby reducing his own authority—yet the eunuchs never stopped spreading calumny against him.
units.literal: He also requested abolishing the business of the Bureau of Military Affairs and returning each office to its original department, to lighten his power—yet the eunuchs ceaselessly fabricated slander.

units.zh: 三年，堅乞罷兼領節鉞，許之。
units.en: In the third year of Tongguang, he firmly petitioned to relinquish his concurrent military governorship, and the emperor granted his request.
units.literal: In the third year, he firmly petitioned to resign his concurrent command of the military commission; permission was granted.

units.zh: 〈（《冊府元龜》云：同光中，崇韜再表辭鎮，批答曰：「朕以卿久司樞要，常處重難。
units.en: (The Cefu Yuangui records: During the Tongguang reign, Guo Chongtao twice memorialized requesting relief from his frontier command. The throne replied in rescript: 'You have long held the keys of state and borne me through grave crises.
units.literal: (The Cefu Yuangui states: During the Tongguang era, Chongtao again submitted a memorial declining his provincial command. An edict in reply read: 'Because you, sir, have long managed vital secrets and constantly stood in difficult and weighty positions.

units.zh: 或遲疑未決之機，詢諸先見；
units.en: When I lingered uncertain at the crossroads, I looked to your foresight;
units.literal: Whenever occasions arose of hesitation where I had not yet decided, I would consult your foresight;

units.zh: 或憂撓不定之事，訪自必成。
units.en: when affairs disturbed my judgment, I asked your counsel and found it always proved true.
units.literal: whenever matters unsettled me and left me undecided, I sought counsel and relied on your sure success.

units.zh: 至於讚朕丕基，登茲大寶，眾興異論，卿獨堅言，天命不可違，唐祚必須復，請納家族，明設誓文，及其密取汶陽，興師入不測之地；
units.en: When I was raised upon the throne, the court was divided in opinion, yet you alone insisted that Heaven's mandate was not to be resisted and the House of Tang must be restored, pledging your own kin and binding us with solemn oaths; when you secretly secured Wenyang and marched into the unknown;
units.literal: As for praising my great foundation and ascending this great treasure, when many raised differing opinions, you alone spoke firmly that the Mandate of Heaven could not be violated, the Tang succession must be restored, offering your family and explicitly setting forth sworn documents; and when you secretly took Wenyang, raised troops, and entered uncertain territory;

units.zh: 潛通河口，貢謀占必濟之津。
units.en: when you opened secret routes at Hekou and laid plans for the ford that had to hold.
units.literal: covertly opening communications at Hekou, submitting plans and divining the crossing that would surely succeed.

units.zh: 人所不知，卿惟合意。
units.en: What remained hidden from others, you alone understood as I meant it.
units.literal: What others did not know, you alone grasped my intent.

units.zh: 迨中都嘯聚，群黨窺陵，朕決議平妖，兼收浚水，雖雲先定，更審前籌，果盡讚成，悉諧沈算，斯即何須冒刃，始顯殊庸。
units.en: When rebellion howled at Zhongdu and traitors cast hungry eyes upon the imperial tombs, I resolved to crush the rebels and recover the Jun River. Though victory seemed already assured, I weighed again your earlier design—and found every outcome matched your praise and your deepest reckoning. What need, then, to risk the blade before your uncommon merit stood plain?
units.literal: When at Zhongdu rebels gathered howling and factions eyed the imperial tombs, I resolved to suppress the demons and also recover the Jun River. Though this was said to be settled in advance, I further examined your earlier planning—the results fully matched your commendations and accorded with your deep calculations. Why then need to brave blades before your exceptional merit was shown?

units.zh: 況常山陸梁，正虞未復，卿能撫眾，共定群心，惟朕知卿，他人寧表。
units.en: Moreover, while Changshan still raged in revolt and Zhenzhou remained unredeemed, you soothed the people and steadied every heart. I alone know what you are worth; who else would dare speak for you?
units.literal: Moreover, Changshan was recalcitrant and Zhenzhou had not yet been recovered. You were able to pacify the masses and together settle all hearts. Only I know you, sir—how could others presume to speak?

units.zh: 所以賞卿之龐，實異等倫；
units.en: The rewards I heaped upon you were without equal among men;
units.literal: Therefore the bounty granted you, sir, is truly without peer;

units.zh: 沃朕之心，非虛渥澤。
units.en: They have warmed my heart, and were no empty grace.
units.literal: They moisten my heart—no empty beneficence.

units.zh: 今卿再三謙遜，重疊退辭，始納常陽，請歸上將，又稱梁苑，不可兼權。
units.en: Now you beg off again and again, asking to yield command after command—willing to keep only Changshan, willing to surrender your rank as chief general, insisting that the Liang Garden command cannot be held with other posts.
units.literal: Now you have repeatedly been modest, layering requests to withdraw—accepting only Changshan, requesting return as supreme general, and again stating that Liangyuan cannot be held concurrently.

units.zh: 如此周身，貴全名節，古人操守，未可比方，既覽堅辭，難沮來表。
units.en: Such care for one's standing, such hunger to preserve name and integrity—no paragon of antiquity could match it. Having read your earnest resignations, I cannot easily refuse what you now submit.
units.literal: Such self-protection, honoring and preserving reputation and integrity—ancient men's integrity cannot be compared. Having reviewed your firm declinations, I find it hard to thwart your petition.

units.zh: 其再讓汴州，所宜依允。」）〉
units.en: Your renewed request to relinquish Bianzhou should be granted as you ask.')〉
units.literal: Regarding your renewed request to yield Bianzhou, permission is rightfully granted.')〉

units.zh: 會客省使李嚴使西川回，言王衍可圖之狀，莊宗與崇韜議討伐之謀，方擇大將。
units.en: About then Guest Affairs Commissioner Li Yan returned from his mission to the West River circuit and reported that Wang Yan's realm was ripe for conquest. Emperor Zhuangzong and Guo Chongtao debated the campaign and were still choosing a commander.
units.literal: It happened that Guest Affairs Commissioner Li Yan returned from his mission to Xichuan, reporting that Wang Yan's situation made him vulnerable to attack. Zhuangzong and Chongtao discussed plans for an expedition and were just selecting a commander.

units.zh: 時明宗為諸道兵馬總管當行，崇韜自以宦者相傾，欲立大功以製之，乃奏曰：「契丹犯邊，北面須藉大臣，全倚總管鎮禦。
units.en: At the time Li Siyuan, as overall commander of the armies of all circuits, was slated to lead the campaign. Guo Chongtao, knowing the eunuchs were working against him, sought a great victory with which to restrain them. He memorialized: "The Khitans are raiding the frontier; the northern line must rest on a senior minister—the overall commander is needed there to hold the defense.
units.literal: At the time Mingzong was overall commander of the armies of all circuits and was slated to lead the campaign. Chongtao, considering how the eunuchs were undermining him, wished to achieve a great victory to check them. He memorialized: "The Khitans are violating the border; the northern front must rely on a senior minister—the overall commander must fully depend on military defense there.

units.zh: 臣伏念興聖宮使繼岌，德望日隆，大功未著，宜依故事，以親王為元帥，付以討伐之權，俾成其威望。」
units.en: I reflect that the Director of the Xingsheng Palace, Li Jiji, grows daily in stature and reputation, yet has not won a great victory of his own. Precedent calls for an imperial prince as commander-in-chief, entrusted with the power of expedition, so that his authority may be established."
units.literal: Your subject reflects that the Director of the Xingsheng Palace, Jiji, grows daily in virtue and reputation, yet has not yet displayed great achievement. According to precedent, a prince should serve as commander-in-chief, entrusted with authority for the expedition, so that his prestige may be established."

units.zh: 莊宗方愛繼岌，即曰：「小兒幼稚，安能獨行，卿當擇其副。」
units.en: Emperor Zhuangzong, who doted on Jiji, said at once: "The boy is still young. How could he go alone? You must choose his deputy."
units.literal: Zhuangzong, who doted on Jiji, immediately said: "The boy is still young—how could he go alone? You must choose his deputy."

units.zh: 崇韜未奏，莊宗曰：「無逾於卿者。」
units.en: Before Guo Chongtao could answer, the emperor said: "There is no one better suited than you."
units.literal: Before Chongtao could reply, Zhuangzong said: "No one surpasses you."

units.zh: 乃以繼岌為都統，崇韜為招討使。
units.en: Jiji was appointed overall commander, and Guo Chongtao Pacification Commissioner.
units.literal: Thereupon Jiji was made overall commander and Chongtao was made Pacification Commissioner.

units.zh: 是歲九月十八日，率親軍六萬，進討蜀川。
units.en: That year, on the eighteenth day of the ninth month, he led sixty thousand imperial guards west against Shu.
units.literal: That year, on the eighteenth day of the ninth month, he led sixty thousand of the imperial guard in an expedition against Shu.

units.zh: 崇韜將發，奏曰：「臣以非才，謬當戎事，仗將士之忠力，憑陛下之威靈，庶幾克捷。
units.en: As Guo Chongtao was about to depart, he memorialized: "I am unworthy and have been wrongly placed in command of war. Trusting in the loyalty and strength of the troops and in Your Majesty's august power, I hope we may prevail.
units.literal: As Chongtao was about to depart, he memorialized: "Your subject, lacking talent, has been wrongly entrusted with military affairs. Relying on the loyalty and strength of officers and soldiers and on Your Majesty's august authority, I hope we may achieve victory.

units.zh: 若西川平定，陛下擇帥，如信厚善謀，事君有節，則孟知祥有焉，望以蜀帥授之。
units.en: If the West River circuit is pacified and Your Majesty chooses a governor—one loyal, trustworthy, prudent in counsel, and restrained in service—Meng Zhixiang is such a man. I ask that the Shu command be given to him.
units.literal: If the western circuit is pacified and Your Majesty selects a commander—one who is trustworthy, generous, skilled in planning, and serves his lord with proper restraint—Meng Zhixiang is such a man. I hope he may be granted the Shu command.

units.zh: 如宰輔闕人，張憲有披榛之勞，為人謹重而多識。
units.en: If the chief ministers need filling, Zhang Xian cleared the thorns at the founding and is a man of gravity, prudence, and wide learning.
units.literal: If the chief ministers lack a worthy candidate, Zhang Xian rendered service in clearing the path at the outset; he is prudent, grave, and widely knowledgeable.

units.zh: 其次李琪、崔居儉，中朝士族，富有文學，可擇而任之。」
units.en: Next are Li Qi and Cui Jujian, eminent clansmen of the central court, men of literary accomplishment who may be chosen and appointed."
units.literal: Next are Li Qi and Cui Jujian, eminent clansmen of the central court, rich in literary skill—they may be selected and appointed."

units.zh: 莊宗禦嘉慶殿，置酒宴征西諸將，舉酒屬崇韜曰：「繼岌未習軍政，卿久從吾戰伐，西面之事，屬之於卿。」
units.en: Emperor Zhuangzong held court in the Jiaqing Hall and feasted the generals bound for the west. Raising his cup to Guo Chongtao, he said: "Jiji has not yet learned the arts of war. You have long marched at my side. The western campaign is yours to command."
units.literal: Zhuangzong held court at the Jiaqing Hall, set out wine and feasted the generals of the western expedition. Raising his cup he addressed Chongtao: "Jiji is not yet versed in military affairs. You have long followed me in campaign. The western enterprise is entrusted to you."

units.zh: 軍發，十月十九日入大散關，崇韜以馬箠指山險謂魏王曰：「朝廷興師十萬，已入此中，儻不成功，安有歸路？
units.en: The army marched out. On the nineteenth day of the tenth month they entered Dasan Pass. Guo Chongtao pointed with his riding crop at the treacherous mountains and said to the Prince of Wei: "The court has sent a hundred thousand men into this trap. If we fail here, what road home remains?
units.literal: The army set out. On the nineteenth day of the tenth month they entered Dasan Pass. Chongtao pointed with his riding crop at the perilous mountains and said to the Prince of Wei: "The court has raised an army of a hundred thousand and already entered these depths. If we do not succeed, what road of return remains?

units.zh: 今岐下飛挽，才支旬日，必須先取鳳州，收其儲積，方濟吾事。」
units.en: Supplies rushed up from beneath Qi will barely last ten days. We must take Fengzhou first and seize its stores, or our cause is lost."
units.literal: Now supplies rushed from beneath Qi barely last ten days. We must first take Fengzhou and seize its stored provisions before our enterprise can succeed."

units.zh: 乃令李嚴、康延孝先馳書檄，以諭偽鳳州節度使王承捷。
units.en: He then ordered Li Yan and Kang Yanxiao to ride ahead with letters and proclamations to summon the puppet Fengzhou military commissioner Wang Chengjie.
units.literal: He then ordered Li Yan and Kang Yanxiao to ride ahead with letters and proclamations to persuade the pseudo-Fengzhou Military Commissioner Wang Chengjie.

units.zh: 及大軍至，承捷果以城降，得兵八千，軍儲四十萬。
units.en: When the main army arrived, Chengjie surrendered the city as expected, yielding eight thousand troops and four hundred thousand units of provisions.
units.literal: When the main army arrived, Chengjie duly surrendered the city, yielding eight thousand troops and four hundred thousand units of military stores.

units.zh: 次至故鎮，偽命屯駐指揮使唐景思亦以城降，得兵四千。
units.en: Next they reached Guzhen, where Tang Jingsi, the garrison commander appointed by the puppet court, also surrendered the city and yielded four thousand troops.
units.literal: Next they reached Guzhen. Tang Jingsi, the garrison commander appointed by the pseudo-court, also surrendered the city, yielding four thousand troops.

units.zh: 又下三泉，得軍儲三十餘萬。
units.en: They then took Sanquan and obtained more than three hundred thousand units of provisions.
units.literal: They then descended upon Sanquan and obtained more than three hundred thousand units of military stores.

units.zh: 自是師無匱乏，軍聲大振。
units.en: From then on the army lacked nothing, and its martial renown swelled.
units.literal: From then on the army wanted for nothing, and its martial reputation greatly rose.

units.zh: 其招懷製置，官吏補置，師行籌畫，軍書告諭，皆出於崇韜，繼岌承命而已。
units.en: Recruitment and pacification, administrative arrangements, filling official posts, planning the march, and drafting orders and proclamations—all came from Guo Chongtao. Li Jiji merely received and carried out his commands.
units.literal: Recruitment and pacification, administrative arrangements, filling official posts, planning the march, and drafting military orders and proclamations—all issued from Chongtao. Jiji merely received and carried out commands.

units.zh: 莊宗令內官李廷安、李從襲、呂知柔為都統府紀綱，見崇韜幕府繁重，將吏輻輳，降人爭先賂遺，都統府唯大將省謁，牙門索然，由是大為詬恥。
units.en: Emperor Zhuangzong appointed the eunuchs Li Ting'an, Li Congxi, and Lü Zhirou as disciplinarians of the overall command headquarters. They saw Guo Chongtao's headquarters thronged with officers and clerks, with surrendered men vying to offer bribes, while the prince's own headquarters received only the chief generals on formal visits and its gate stood empty. They were deeply shamed.
units.literal: Emperor Zhuangzong appointed the eunuchs Li Ting'an, Li Congxi, and Lü Zhirou as disciplinarians of the overall command headquarters. Seeing Chongtao's headquarters heavy with business, officers and clerks crowding in, and surrendered men vying to offer bribes, while the headquarters saw only the chief generals on formal visits and its gate stood empty—they were deeply shamed.

units.zh: 及六軍使王宗弼歸款，行賂先招討府。
units.en: When Wang Zongbi, commander of the Six Armies, came over to the Tang side, he sent bribes first to the Pacification Commissioner's headquarters.
units.literal: When Wang Zongbi, commander of the Six Armies, submitted allegiance, he offered bribes first to the Pacification Commissioner's headquarters.

units.zh: 王衍以成都降，崇韜居王宗弼之第。
units.en: When Wang Yan surrendered Chengdu, Guo Chongtao took up residence in Wang Zongbi's mansion.
units.literal: When Wang Yan surrendered Chengdu, Chongtao took up residence in Wang Zongbi's mansion.

units.zh: 宗弼選王衍之妓妾珍玩以奉崇韜，求為蜀帥，崇韜許之。
units.en: Zongbi selected Wang Yan's courtesans and treasures to present to Guo Chongtao and asked to be made governor of Shu; Chongtao agreed.
units.literal: Zongbi selected Wang Yan's courtesans and precious objects to present to Chongtao, requesting appointment as Shu commander; Chongtao agreed.

units.zh: 又與崇韜子廷誨謀，令蜀人列狀見魏王，請奏崇韜為蜀帥。
units.en: He also plotted with Guo Chongtao's son Tinghui to have men of Shu submit collective petitions to the Prince of Wei asking that a memorial be sent appointing Guo Chongtao governor of Shu.
units.literal: He also plotted with Chongtao's son Tinghui to have men of Shu submit collective petitions to the Prince of Wei requesting that a memorial be sent appointing Chongtao Shu commander.

units.zh: 繼岌覽狀謂崇韜曰：「主上倚侍中如衡、華，安肯棄元老於蠻夷之地，況餘不敢議此。」
units.en: Jiji read the petitions and said to Guo Chongtao: "His Majesty relies on you as on Mount Heng and Mount Hua—how would he cast a senior minister off into barbarian country? As for me, I dare not even speak of such a thing."
units.literal: Jiji read the petitions and said to Chongtao: "His Majesty relies on you, Minister, as on Mount Heng and Mount Hua—how would he abandon a senior minister in barbarian lands? As for me, I dare not broach such a matter."

units.zh: 〈（《九國誌·王宗弼傳》：宗弼送款於魏王，乃還成都，盡輦內藏之寶貨，歸於其家。
units.en: (Biography of Wang Zongbi in the Jiuguo Zhi: After Zongbi submitted allegiance to the Prince of Wei, he returned to Chengdu and carted off all the treasures of the inner treasury to his own house.
units.literal: (Biography of Wang Zongbi in the Jiuguo Zhi: After Zongbi submitted allegiance to the Prince of Wei, he returned to Chengdu and transported all treasures of the inner treasury to his own home.

units.zh: 魏王遣使征犒軍錢數千萬，宗弼輒靳之，魏王甚怒。
units.en: The Prince of Wei sent envoys to levy several tens of millions in cash to reward the army, but Zongbi repeatedly refused, and the prince was furious.
units.literal: The Prince of Wei sent envoys to levy several tens of millions in funds to reward the army; Zongbi consistently withheld them, and the Prince was greatly angered.

units.zh: 及王師至，令其子承班齎衍玩用直百萬，獻於魏王，並賂郭崇韜，請以己為西川節度使。
units.en: When the imperial army arrived, he had his son Chengbian bring Wang Yan's playthings worth a million in cash, present them to the Prince of Wei, and also bribe Guo Chongtao, asking to be made military commissioner of the West River circuit.
units.literal: When the imperial army arrived, he had his son Chengbian bring playthings of Wang Yan worth a million in cash, present them to the Prince of Wei, and also bribe Guo Chongtao, requesting appointment as Military Commissioner of Xichuan.

units.zh: 魏王曰：「此吾家之物，焉用獻為！」
units.en: The Prince of Wei said: "These are things of my own house—why offer them as gifts!"
units.literal: The Prince of Wei said: "These are possessions of my house—why present them as gifts!"

units.zh: 魏王入城，翌日，數其不忠之罪，並其子斬之於市。）〉
units.en: The day after the prince entered the city, he enumerated Zongbi's crimes of disloyalty and executed him and his son in the marketplace.)〉
units.literal: The next day after the Prince entered the city, he enumerated his crimes of disloyalty and executed him and his son in the marketplace.)〉

units.zh: 李從襲等謂繼岌曰：「郭公收蜀部人情，意在難測，王宜自備。」
units.en: Li Congxi and the others said to Jiji: "Minister Guo has won over the people of Shu, and his intentions are hard to read. Your Highness should be on your guard."
units.literal: Li Congxi and others said to Jiji: "Minister Guo has won the hearts of Shu; his intentions are hard to fathom. Your Highness should guard yourself."

units.zh: 由是兩相猜察。
units.en: From this mutual suspicion took hold between them.
units.literal: From this the two sides mutually suspected and watched each other.

units.zh: 莊宗令中官向延嗣齎詔至蜀，促班師，詔使至，崇韜不郊迎，延嗣憤憤。
units.en: Emperor Zhuangzong sent the eunuch Xiang Yansi to Shu with an edict ordering the army's return. When the imperial messenger arrived, Guo Chongtao failed to greet him with the customary ceremony at the city outskirts, and Yansi was incensed.
units.literal: Emperor Zhuangzong ordered the eunuch Xiang Yansi to carry an edict to Shu urging withdrawal of the army. When the edict envoy arrived, Chongtao did not go out to meet him in the suburbs, and Yansi was furious.

units.zh: 從襲謂之曰：「魏王，貴太子也，主上萬福，郭公專弄威柄，旁若無人。
units.en: Li Congxi said to him, "The Prince of Wei is the heir apparent—while the emperor enjoys every blessing under heaven, Lord Guo wields power alone and carries himself as though the rest of us did not exist.
units.literal: Congxi said to him, "The Prince of Wei is the precious heir apparent, and Our Lord enjoys ten thousand blessings, yet Lord Guo monopolizes power and acts as though no one else were present.

units.zh: 昨令蜀人請己為帥，郭廷誨擁徒出入，貴擬王者，所與狎遊，無非軍中驍果，蜀中凶豪，晝夜妓樂歡宴，指天畫地，父子如此，可見其心。
units.en: Just yesterday they had the people of Shu petition to make him regional commander. Guo Tinghui travels about surrounded by his own followers, carrying himself almost like a king. His companions are the army's boldest fighters and Shu's most dangerous ruffians. Day and night the two hold banquets of wine, music, and women, swearing reckless oaths with grand gestures—and from such conduct, father and son alike, their ambitions are plain.
units.literal: Yesterday they had Shu people petition that he himself be made regional commander. Guo Tinghui goes in and out surrounded by retainers, his status rivaling that of royalty. Those with whom they carouse are none other than the army's fiercest fighters and Shu's violent magnates. Day and night they revel with music and courtesans, swearing oaths with pointed fingers—father and son conduct themselves thus; their intent is plain to see.

units.zh: 今諸軍將校，無非郭氏之黨，魏王懸軍孤弱，一朝班師，必恐紛亂，吾屬莫知暴骨之所！」
units.en: Every officer in the army now seems to belong to the Guo faction. The Prince of Wei is stranded far from home with only a slender force. Once we withdraw, chaos is all but certain—and we may never know where our bones will be left to rot!"
units.literal: Now the officers of all armies are without exception partisans of the Guo clan. The Prince of Wei is left with an isolated army in enemy country—once withdrawal is ordered, turmoil is certain to follow, and we cannot know where our bones will lie unburied!"

units.zh: 因相向垂涕。
units.en: They broke down in tears as they faced one another.
units.literal: Thereupon they wept facing each other.

units.zh: 延嗣使還具奏，皇后泣告莊宗，乞保全繼岌。
units.en: Yansi reported everything on his return. The empress wept before Emperor Zhuangzong and begged him to protect Li Jiji.
units.literal: When Yansi returned from his mission he submitted a full report. The empress tearfully told Emperor Zhuangzong and begged that Jiji be kept safe.

units.zh: 莊宗復閱蜀簿曰：「人言蜀中珠玉金銀，不知其數，何如是之微也！」
units.en: Emperor Zhuangzong again reviewed the Shu account books and said, "Everyone says the pearls, jade, gold, and silver of Shu are beyond numbering—how can the tally be so small?"
units.literal: Emperor Zhuangzong again reviewed the Shu ledger and said, "People say the pearls, jade, gold, and silver of Shu are beyond counting—how can the amounts be so small!"

units.zh: 延嗣奏曰：「臣問蜀人，知蜀中寶貨皆入崇韜之門，言崇韜得金萬兩，銀四十萬，名馬千匹，王衍愛妓六十，樂工百，犀玉帶百。
units.en: Yansi reported, "I questioned people in Shu and learned that the region's treasures had all passed through Guo Chongtao's hands. They say he took ten thousand liang of gold, four hundred thousand of silver, a thousand fine horses, sixty of Wang Yan's favorite concubines, a hundred musicians, and a hundred rhinoceros-horn and jade belts.
units.literal: Yansi memorialized, saying, "Your servant asked Shu people and learned that all precious goods of Shu entered Chongtao's household. It is said Chongtao obtained ten thousand liang of gold, four hundred thousand of silver, a thousand famous horses, sixty of Wang Yan's favorite courtesans, a hundred musicians, and a hundred rhinoceros-horn and jade belts.

units.zh: 廷誨自有金銀十萬兩，犀玉帶五十，藝色絕妓七十，樂工七十，他財稱是。
units.en: Guo Tinghui personally held a hundred thousand liang in gold and silver, fifty rhinoceros-horn and jade belts, seventy courtesans of rare beauty and talent, seventy musicians, and comparable riches besides.
units.literal: Tinghui personally possessed a hundred thousand liang of gold and silver, fifty rhinoceros-horn and jade belts, seventy courtesans of exceptional skill and beauty, seventy musicians, and comparable other wealth.

units.zh: 魏王府，蜀人賂遺不過遣匹馬而已。」
units.en: As for the Prince of Wei's household, gifts from Shu amounted to little more than the loan of a horse."
units.literal: At the Prince of Wei's residence, Shu people's gifts amounted to no more than the loan of a horse."

units.zh: 莊宗初聞崇韜欲留蜀，心已不平，又聞全有蜀之妓樂珍玩，怒見顏色。
units.en: Emperor Zhuangzong had already resented the rumor that Guo Chongtao meant to stay in Shu; when he heard next that Chongtao had taken for himself all the region's courtesans, musicians, and treasures, his anger was plain on his face.
units.literal: When Emperor Zhuangzong first heard that Chongtao wished to remain in Shu, his heart was already displeased. When he further heard that Chongtao possessed all of Shu's courtesans, musicians, and treasures, anger showed in his countenance.

units.zh: 即令中官馬彥珪馳入蜀視崇韜去就，如班師則已，如實遲留，則與繼岌圖之。
units.en: He immediately dispatched the eunuch Ma Yan'gui to Shu to learn whether Guo Chongtao intended to withdraw. If Chongtao returned with the army, nothing more need be done; if he truly meant to linger, Yan'gui was to join Li Jiji in removing him.
units.literal: He immediately ordered the eunuch Ma Yan'gui to ride posthaste into Shu to observe whether Chongtao would withdraw. If he withdrew with the army, that would be the end of it; if he truly delayed, then Yan'gui was to plot with Jiji against him.

units.zh: 彥珪見皇后曰：「禍機之發，間不容發，何能數千里外復稟聖旨哉！」
units.en: Ma Yan'gui told the empress, "When disaster is about to strike, not a moment can be wasted—how can we seek fresh orders from thousands of li away?"
units.literal: Yan'gui saw the empress and said, "When calamity is about to break out, not a hair's breadth of time can be spared—how can one seek imperial edict again from thousands of li away!"

units.zh: 皇后再言之，莊宗曰：「未知事之實否，詎可便令果決？」
units.en: The empress pressed the point again. Emperor Zhuangzong said, "We do not yet know whether any of this is true—how can we order so fatal a step on hearsay alone?"
units.literal: The empress spoke again, and Emperor Zhuangzong said, "We do not yet know whether the matter is true—how can we immediately order so decisive an act?"

units.zh: 皇后乃自為教與繼岌，令殺崇韜。
units.en: The empress then wrote her own order to Li Jiji commanding Guo Chongtao's death.
units.literal: The empress then herself wrote an order to Jiji commanding that Chongtao be killed.

units.zh: 時蜀土初平，山林多盜，孟知祥未至，崇韜令任圜、張筠分道招撫，慮師還後，部曲不寧，故歸期稍緩。
units.en: Shu had only just been pacified; bandits still roamed the hills, and Meng Zhixiang had not yet arrived. Guo Chongtao sent Ren Yuan and Zhang Jun along separate routes to win over and settle the countryside, fearing unrest among his followers once the army withdrew—hence the slight delay in their return.
units.literal: At that time Shu had only recently been pacified, bandits were numerous in the mountains and forests, and Meng Zhixiang had not yet arrived. Chongtao ordered Ren Yuan and Zhang Jun to pacify the people by separate routes, fearing that after the army returned his followers would not remain settled—therefore the date of return was slightly delayed.

units.zh: 四年正月六日，馬彥珪至軍，決取十二日發成都赴闕，令任圜權知留事，以俟知祥。
units.en: On the sixth day of the first month of the fourth year, Ma Yan'gui reached headquarters. They set the twelfth as the day to march from Chengdu for the capital, left Ren Yuan in charge of local affairs, and waited for Meng Zhixiang.
units.literal: On the sixth day of the first month of the fourth year, Ma Yan'gui reached the army. They fixed the twelfth as the day to depart Chengdu for the capital. Ren Yuan was left to act as provisional administrator pending Zhixiang's arrival.

units.zh: 諸軍部署已定，彥珪出皇后教以示繼岌，繼岌曰：「大軍將發，他無釁端，安得為此負心事！
units.en: With the army's dispositions complete, Yan'gui showed Li Jiji the empress's order. Li Jiji said, "The army is on the eve of departure, and there is no other provocation—how can I commit so shameful an act!
units.literal: Once the army's deployment was settled, Yan'gui produced the empress's order and showed it to Jiji. Jiji said, "The great army is about to march. There is no other cause for trouble—how can I do this shameful deed!

units.zh: 公輩勿復言。」
units.en: Say no more of it."
units.literal: You gentlemen need speak no more of this."

units.zh: 從襲等泣曰：「聖上既有口敕，王若不行，苟中途事泄，為患轉深。」
units.en: Li Congxi and the others wept and said, "The emperor has already given the command by word of mouth. If you refuse and the plot leaks midway, the consequences will only grow worse."
units.literal: Congxi and the others wept and said, "Since the Holy Sovereign has already given an oral command, if Your Highness does not act and the matter should leak out midway, the harm will grow only deeper."

units.zh: 繼岌曰：「上無詔書，徒以皇后教令，安得殺招討使！」
units.en: Li Jiji said, "There is no imperial edict—only the empress's order. How can I kill the expeditionary commander!"
units.literal: Jiji said, "There is no imperial edict from above—only the empress's order. How can I kill the commander-in-chief!"

units.zh: 從襲等巧造事端以間之，繼岌既英斷，僶俛從之。
units.en: Li Congxi and the others artfully manufactured provocations to destroy trust between them. Though Li Jiji was resolute by nature, in the end he bowed to their pressure and agreed.
units.literal: Congxi and the others craftily fabricated incidents to drive a wedge between them. Jiji, though resolute by nature, reluctantly consented.

units.zh: 詰旦，從襲以繼岌之命召崇韜計事，繼岌登樓避之，崇韜入，左右楇殺之。
units.en: At dawn Li Congxi, acting on Li Jiji's orders, summoned Guo Chongtao to discuss business. Li Jiji climbed a tower to keep his distance. When Chongtao entered, attendants clubbed him to death.
units.literal: At dawn Congxi, on Jiji's order, summoned Chongtao to discuss affairs. Jiji ascended a tower to avoid the scene. When Chongtao entered, attendants beat him to death with clubs.

units.zh: 崇韜有子五人，廷信、廷誨隨父死於蜀，廷說誅於洛陽，廷讓誅於魏州，廷議誅於太原，家產籍沒。
units.en: Guo Chongtao had five sons. Tingxin and Tinghui died with their father in Shu. Tingshuo was executed in Luoyang, Tingrang at Weizhou, and Tingyi at Taiyuan. The family's estates were confiscated.
units.literal: Chongtao had five sons. Tingxin and Tinghui died with their father in Shu. Tingshuo was executed in Luoyang, Tingrang at Weizhou, and Tingyi at Taiyuan. The family's property was confiscated and listed.

units.zh: 明宗即位，詔令歸葬，仍賜太原舊宅。
units.en: When Emperor Mingzong took the throne, he ordered Guo Chongtao reburied with honor and restored the family's former residence in Taiyuan.
units.literal: When Emperor Mingzong ascended the throne, he ordered that Chongtao be reburied with honor and granted his former residence in Taiyuan.

units.zh: 延誨、廷讓各有幼子一人，姻族保之獲免，崇韜妻周氏，攜養於太原。
units.en: Tinghui and Tingrang each left a young son; kinsmen by marriage sheltered them and they were spared. Guo Chongtao's wife, Lady Zhou, took them in and raised them in Taiyuan.
units.literal: Tinghui and Tingrang each had one young son; in-laws protected them and they were spared. Chongtao's wife, Lady Zhou, took them in and raised them in Taiyuan.

units.zh: 崇韜服勤盡節，佐佑王家，草昧艱難，功無與比，西平巴蜀，宣暢皇威，身死之日，夷夏冤之。
units.en: Guo Chongtao had served with tireless loyalty, standing by the royal house through the founding struggle with achievements few could match. He subdued Ba and Shu in the west and carried imperial might to the frontiers. On the day he died, both Chinese and foreigners alike felt his end was unjust.
units.literal: Chongtao served diligently and fulfilled his charge, supporting the royal house through the rough founding of the dynasty with achievements unmatched by any other. He pacified Ba and Shu in the west and spread imperial might abroad. On the day of his death, barbarian and Chinese alike mourned his injustice.

units.zh: 然議者以崇韜功烈雖多，事權太重，不能處身量力，而聽小人誤計，欲取泰山之安，如急行避跡，其禍愈速。
units.en: Yet critics noted that for all his achievements, Guo Chongtao wielded too much power and failed to measure himself against his place. He listened to petty men's bad counsel. Seeking security as unshakable as Mount Tai, he acted like a man fleeing in haste to cover his tracks—and brought ruin upon himself all the faster.
units.literal: Yet commentators held that although Chongtao's achievements were many, his power was too great. Unable to measure himself and act within his means, he listened to petty men's mistaken schemes. Wishing to secure safety as firm as Mount Tai, he acted like one hurrying to hide his tracks—and his calamity came all the swifter.

units.zh: 性復剛戾，遇事便發，既不知前代之成敗，又未體當時之物情，以天下為己任，孟浪之甚也。
units.en: He was stubborn and explosive by nature, ignorant of the rise and fall of earlier dynasties and blind to the mood of his own day, yet he acted as though the realm rested on his shoulders alone—a recklessness bordering on arrogance.
units.literal: His nature was moreover stubborn and harsh; he erupted at every turn. He neither understood the successes and failures of earlier ages nor grasped the temper of the times, yet took the realm upon himself—recklessness in the extreme.

units.zh: 及權傾四海，車騎盈門，士人諂奉，漸別流品。
units.en: Once his power eclipsed all others, his gates overflowed with visitors, scholars flattered him, and he began sorting men by pedigree and rank.
units.literal: Once his power tilted the four seas, chariots and riders filled his gates, scholars fawned upon him, and he gradually sorted people by pedigree.

units.zh: 同列豆盧革謂崇韜曰：「汾陽王代北人，徙家華陰，侍中世在雁門，得非祖德歟？」
units.en: His colleague Doulu Ge said to Guo Chongtao, "The Prince of Fenyang came from northern Dai and moved his family to Huayin. Your family has roots in Yanmen for generations—surely this is ancestral grace?"
units.literal: His colleague Doulu Ge said to Chongtao, "The Prince of Fenyang was a man of northern Dai who moved his family to Huayin. You, Lord Chancellor, have generations in Yanmen—is this not ancestral virtue?"

units.zh: 崇韜應曰：「經亂失譜牒，先人嘗雲去汾陽王四世。」
units.en: Guo Chongtao answered, "The genealogies were lost in the chaos, but our ancestors once said we were four generations from the Prince of Fenyang."
units.literal: Chongtao replied, "Through the turmoil the genealogical records were lost, but our forebears once said we were four generations removed from the Prince of Fenyang."

units.zh: 革曰：「故祖德也。」
units.en: Doulu Ge said, "Then it is indeed ancestral merit."
units.literal: Ge said, "So it is ancestral virtue after all."

units.zh: 因是旌別流品，援引薄徒，委之心腹；
units.en: Thereafter he ranked men by lineage, elevated low-born followers, and entrusted them with his innermost affairs;
units.literal: From this he distinguished pedigree, promoted base companions, and entrusted them as his inner circle;

units.zh: 佐命勳舊，一切鄙棄。
units.en: and founding veterans who had shared the struggle he treated with open contempt.
units.literal: the founding merit-holders and old companions he utterly despised and cast aside.

units.zh: 舊僚有幹進者，崇韜謂之曰：「公雖代邸之舊，然家無門閥，深知公才技，不敢驟進者，慮名流嗤餘故也。」
units.en: When an old colleague sought promotion, Guo Chongtao told him, "You are indeed an old companion from the Prince of Dai's camp, but your family lacks a great lineage. I know well what you can do, yet I dare not advance you hastily for fear the eminent would laugh at me."
units.literal: When an old subordinate sought advancement, Chongtao told him, "Although you are an old companion from the Prince of Dai's household, your family has no great pedigree. Though I well know your talent and skill, I dare not advance you abruptly for fear the leading men would scorn me for it."

units.zh: 及征蜀之行，於興平拜尚父子儀之墓。
units.en: On the march into Shu, he paid his respects at Xingping at the tomb of the Honorary Prince of Guo, Ziyi.
units.literal: On the expedition to Shu, at Xingping he paid respects at the tomb of the Honorary Prince of Guo, Ziyi.

units.zh: 嘗從容白繼岌曰：「蜀平之後，王為太子，待千秋萬歲，神器在手，宜盡去宦官，優禮士族，不唯疏斥閹寺，騸馬不可復乘。」
units.en: He once told Li Jiji in confidence, "When Shu is pacified you will be crown prince, and in the years to come, with the throne in your hand, you should purge the eunuchs and honor the scholar-official clans—not merely ostracize the palace eunuchs, but never again ride a gelded horse."
units.literal: He once calmly told Jiji, "After Shu is pacified you will be crown prince, and when you reign for ten thousand years with the imperial regalia in hand, you should remove all eunuchs, honor the gentry families, not only cast out the palace eunuchs, but never again ride gelded horses."

units.zh: 內則伶官巷伯，怒目切齒；
units.en: Within the court, actor-officials and eunuchs gnashed their teeth in fury;
units.literal: Within, the actor-officials and eunuchs glared and ground their teeth;

units.zh: 外則舊僚宿將，戟手痛心。
units.en: without, veteran officers and old companions wrung their hands in outrage.
units.literal: without, old subordinates and veteran generals pointed in accusation with anguished hearts.

units.zh: 掇其族滅之禍，有自來矣。
units.en: The disaster that wiped out his clan had been gathering long before.
units.literal: That he brought upon himself the calamity of extermination of his clan had long been foreshadowed.

units.zh: 復以諸子驕縱不法，既定蜀川，輦運珍貨，實於洛陽之第，籍沒之日，泥封尚濕。
units.en: His sons, too, were arrogant and lawless. Once Shu was taken, cartloads of treasure were stored in the family's Luoyang mansion—on the day of confiscation the clay seals were still fresh.
units.literal: Moreover his sons were arrogant, unrestrained, and lawless. Once Shu was secured, precious goods were carted and stored in his Luoyang mansion; on the day of confiscation the clay seals were still wet.

units.zh: 雖莊宗季年為群小所惑，致功臣不保其終，亦崇韜自貽其災禍也。
units.en: True, in his final years Emperor Zhuangzong was led astray by petty men, and many a meritorious minister failed to die in peace—but Guo Chongtao also made his own disaster.
units.literal: Although in his final years Emperor Zhuangzong was deluded by petty men, causing meritorious ministers not to keep their ends, Chongtao also brought calamity upon himself.

units.zh: 史臣曰：夫出身事主，得位遭時，功不可以不圖，名不可以不立。
units.en: The historiographer writes: When a man rises from humble station to serve his sovereign and gains office in his time, merit must be sought and renown must be won.
units.literal: The historiographer says: One who leaves humble origins to serve a lord, gains office and meets his time—merit cannot go unplanned, renown cannot go unestablished.

units.zh: 洎功成而名遂，則望重而身危，貝錦於是成文，良玉以之先折，故崇韜之誅，蓋為此也。
units.en: Yet once merit is won and renown secured, great standing invites danger. Slander weaves itself into pattern, fine jade shatters first—and Guo Chongtao's execution, in the main, arose from this.
units.literal: But when merit is achieved and renown fulfilled, then weighty standing brings peril to the person. The brocaded slander takes shape, fine jade is broken first—thus Chongtao's execution was largely for this reason.

units.zh: 是知強吳滅而范蠡去，全齊下而樂生奔，苟非其賢，孰免於禍。
units.en: So we see: when mighty Wu was destroyed, Fan Li withdrew; when all Qi was taken, Lord Yue fled. Unless a man possesses such wisdom, who can escape ruin?
units.literal: From this we know: when mighty Wu fell, Fan Li departed; when all Qi was conquered, Lord Yue fled. If one is not such a man of wisdom, who can escape calamity?

units.zh: 明哲之士，當鑒於斯！
units.en: The wise ought to take this as their warning!
units.literal: The wise and discerning should take this as a mirror!

units.zh: 是時伶人景進用事，閹官競進，故重臣憂懼，拜章請退。
units.en: The actor Jing Jin then held sway and eunuchs crowded forward, so great ministers feared for themselves and begged to step down.
units.literal: At that time the actor Jing Jin held power, and eunuchs vied for advancement; hence the great ministers were fearful and submitted memorials asking to withdraw.

units.zh: 夫種、蠡無一罪，身死亡；
units.en: Wen Zhong and Fan Li had committed no such crimes, yet they still perished.
units.literal: Wen Zhong and Fan Li committed no such crimes, yet they died.

units.zh: 丙子，以北京副留守、太原尹孟知祥為檢校太傅、同平章事、成都尹、劍南西川節度副大使、知節度事、西山八國雲南都招撫等使；
units.en: On bingzi Meng Zhixiang—northern deputy regent and Taiyuan prefect—became acting Grand Tutor, chancellor, Chengdu prefect, Jiannan Xichuan vice commissioner and acting commissioner, and pacification commissioner for the western mountains and Yunnan;
units.literal: On bingzi, northern capital deputy regent and Taiyuan prefect Meng Zhixiang was made acting Grand Tutor, co-equal chief minister, Chengdu prefect, Jiannan Xichuan military vice commissioner, acting commissioner, and commissioner for pacification of the western mountains' eight states and Yunnan and the rest;

units.zh: 中和末，以太原李克用兵勢方盛，與定州王處存密相締結。
units.en: Late in the Zhonghe era, fearing the rising power of Li Keyong of Taiyuan, Keju secretly allied himself with Wang Chucun of Dingzhou.
units.literal: Late in Zhonghe, because Li Keyong of Taiyuan's military power was then flourishing, he secretly formed a pact with Wang Chucun of Dingzhou.

units.zh: 克用怒，加兵討之。
units.en: Keyong was furious and sent additional troops to punish him.
units.literal: Keyong was enraged and added troops to campaign against him.

units.zh: 赫連鐸據雲中，屢引匡威與河東爭雲、代，並兵積年。
units.en: Helian Duo held Yunzhong and repeatedly drew Kuangwei into conflict with Hedong over Yunzhou and Daizhou; their armies fought for years.
units.literal: Helian Duo held Yunzhong and repeatedly drew Kuangwei into contest with Hedong over Yun and Dai; their armies clashed for years.

units.zh: 可舉慮其窺伺山東，終為己患，遂遣使構雲中赫連鐸乘其背，則與鎮州合謀舉兵，兼言易、定是燕、趙之餘，雲得其地則正其疆理而分之。
units.en: Keju feared that Keyong would turn his ambitions toward the eastern provinces and become a lasting threat. He sent envoys to incite Helian Duo of Yunzhong to attack Keyong from the rear, then conspired with the forces of Zhenzhou to raise troops. He argued that Yizhou and Dingzhou were the last holdings of Yan and Zhao, and that if Yunzhong gained those lands their boundaries could be redrawn and the territory divided.
units.literal: Keju feared that Keyong would watch for an opening in the Shandong region and in the end become a threat to him; he therefore sent envoys to incite Helian Duo of Yunzhong to strike from the rear, then conspired with Zhenzhou to raise troops, also saying that Yi and Ding were the remnant territories of Yan and Zhao, and that if Yun gained those lands their boundaries could be rectified and divided.

units.zh: 景福初，鎮州王鎔誘河東將李存孝。
