units.en: Early in the Jingfu era Wang Rong of Zhenzhou won over the Hedong general Li Cunxiao.
units.literal: At the beginning of the Jingfu reign, Wang Rong of Zhenzhou enticed the Hedong general Li Cunxiao.

units.zh: 二年春，河東復出師井陘，再乞師，匡威來援。
units.en: In the spring of the second year Hedong again marched through Jingxing Pass. Wang Rong again appealed for help, and Kuangwei came to his aid.
units.literal: In spring of the second year Hedong again marched out through Jingxing; Rong again begged for troops, and Kuangwei came to his aid.

units.zh: 製以魏國夫人劉氏為皇后，仍令所司擇日備禮冊命。
units.en: Empress Liu of Wei was proclaimed and a day set for full investiture.
units.literal: A pronouncement made Lady Liu of Wei state empress and ordered the relevant office to choose a day and prepare the full investiture rite.

units.zh: 己卯，帝御文明殿，冊魏國夫人劉氏為皇后。
units.en: On jimao Cunxu enfeoffed Lady Liu of Wei as empress at Civilized Hall.
units.literal: On jimao, the Emperor attended Civilized Hall and enfeoffed Lady Liu of Wei as empress.

units.zh: 戊寅，契丹阿保機遣使貢良馬。
units.en: On wuyin Abaoji sent fine horses as tribute.
units.literal: On wuyin the Khitan Abaoji sent envoys presenting fine horses.

units.zh: 時李嗣源總帳下親軍攻東北隅；
units.en: Li Siyuan led the household guard against the northeast corner;
units.literal: Li Siyuan commanded the personal troops below the tent attacking the northeast corner;

units.zh: 李嗣源壞夾城東北隅，率先掩擊，梁軍大恐，南向而奔，投戈委甲，噎塞行路，斬萬餘級，獲其將副招討使符道昭洎大將三百人，芻粟百萬。
units.en: Li Siyuan breached Jiacity's northeast and charged in; Liang panicked and fled south, shedding arms until the road jammed; over ten thousand were killed; Fu Daozhao and three hundred officers were taken, with a million bundles of fodder.
units.literal: Li Siyuan broke the northeast corner of Jiacity and led the assault; the Liang army was greatly terrified and fled south, casting weapons and armor; the road was choked; more than ten thousand were beheaded; deputy pacification commissioner Fu Daozhao and three hundred great generals were captured, and a million measures of fodder.

units.zh: 五月辛未朔，晨霧晦暝，帝率親軍伏三垂崗下。
units.en: At the xinwei new moon in the fifth month, thick morning fog hid Cunxu's personal troops below Sanchui Ridge.
units.literal: On the first day xinwei of the fifth month, morning fog dark and dim, the Emperor led his personal army in ambush below Sanchui Ridge.

units.zh: 六月，遣兗州節度使劉鄩、華州節度使尹皓、崇州節度使溫昭圖、莊宅使段凝領軍攻同州。
units.en: In the sixth month Liu Yan of Yan, Yin Hao of Hua, Wen Zhaotu of Chong, and Duan Ning of the Manor Estates marched on Tongzhou.
units.literal: In the sixth month, Yanzhou military commissioner Liu Yan, Huazhou military commissioner Yin Hao, Chongzhou military commissioner Wen Zhaotu, and Manor Estates commissioner Duan Ning led armies to attack Tongzhou.

units.zh: 八月，段凝、張朗攻衛州，下之，獲刺史李存儒以獻。
units.en: In the eighth month Duan Ning and Zhang Lang took Weizhou and sent captive commissioner Li Cunru to court.
units.literal: In the eighth month Duan Ning and Zhang Lang attacked Weizhou and took it, capturing military commissioner Li Cunru and presenting him.

units.zh: 己巳，王彥章、段凝圍楊劉城。
units.en: On jisi Wang Yanzhang and Duan Ning besieged Yangliu.
units.literal: On jisi, Wang Yanzhang and Duan Ning besieged Yangliu city.

units.zh: 八月，以段凝代王彥章為北面行營招討使。
units.en: In the eighth month Duan Ning replaced Wang Yanzhang as northern commander.
units.literal: In the eighth month Duan Ning replaced Wang Yanzhang as Northern Campaign Pacification commissioner.

units.zh: 戊子，段凝營於王村，引軍自高陵渡河，復臨河而還。
units.en: On wuzi Duan Ning camped at Wang village, crossed at Gaoling, and maneuvered along the river.
units.literal: On wuzi, Duan Ning encamped at Wang village, led troops from Gaoling to cross the river, and again faced the river returning.

units.zh: 帝聞中都之敗，唐軍長驅將至，遣張漢倫馳驛召段凝於河上；
units.en: Hearing of Zhongdu’s fall and Tang’s advance, the Emperor dispatched Zhang Hanlun to recall Duan Ning from the river;
units.literal: The Emperor heard of Zhongdu’s defeat and that Tang troops were coming at speed; he sent Zhang Hanlun by post relay to summon Duan Ning on the river;

units.zh: 時禁軍尚有四千人，朱圭請以拒唐軍，帝不從，登建國門召開封尹王瓚，謂之曰：「段凝未至，社稷係卿方略。」
units.en: Four thousand guards remained; Zhu Gui begged to fight; the Emperor refused, climbed the Founding Gate, called Wang Zan, and said: "Until Duan Ning comes the realm rests on you."
units.literal: At the time the Imperial Guard still had four thousand men; Zhu Gui asked to use them to resist Tang troops; the Emperor did not follow, ascended the Founding Gate, summoned Kaifeng Intendant Wang Zan, and said to him: "Duan Ning has not arrived—the altars depend on your strategy."

units.zh: 辛卯，以宣徽南院使、判內侍省、兼內局、特進、左監門將軍同正李紹宏為右領軍衛上將軍。
units.en: On xinmao Li Shaohong—Southern Secretariat attendant, Inner Palace overseer, Special Grandee, and Left Gate Guard general—became senior general of the Right Guard.
units.literal: On xinmao, Palace Attendant of the Southern Court of the Palace Secretariat, overseer of the Inner Palace, concurrent Inner Bureau, Special Grandee, and Left Gate Guard general of the same rank Li Shaohong was made senior general of the Right Imperial Guard.

units.zh: 樞密使張居翰聞之怒，謂希甫曰：「老夫曆事三朝天子，見內宴數百，子本田舍兒，安知宮禁事！」
units.en: Commissioner Zhang Juhan flew into a rage: "I have served three emperors and attended hundreds of inner banquets—you're a country bumpkin; what do you know of palace protocol!"
units.literal: The commissioner Zhang Juhan heard this and grew angry; he said to Xifu: "This old man has served three dynasties of Son of Heaven and witnessed hundreds of inner banquets—you, a rustic farm boy, what do you know of palace regulations!"

units.zh: 同光初，有詔定內宴儀，問希甫樞密使得坐否，希甫以為不可。
units.en: Early in the Tongguang era, when court protocol for inner banquets was being set, he was asked whether the commissioner of military affairs should have a seat; Xifu said no.
units.literal: At the beginning of the Tongguang era an edict was issued to fix the protocol for inner banquets; Xifu was asked whether the commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs might be seated, and he said it was not permissible.

units.zh: 初，莊宗欲以希甫知制誥，宰相豆盧革等附居翰，共排斥之，以為駕部郎中。
units.en: Zhuangzong had wanted to make him a drafter of edicts, but Chief Ministers Doulu Ge and others, siding with Zhang Juhan, blocked him and gave him only a post as director in the Transport Department.
units.literal: Earlier Zhuangzong had wished to make Xifu drafter of edicts; the chief ministers Dou Luge and others sided with Zhang Juhan and jointly pushed him aside, appointing him director in the Department of Transport.

units.zh: 以鄴都副留守、興唐尹張憲檢校吏部尚書、太原尹，充北京副留守、知留守事。
units.en: Zhang Xian—Yedu deputy regent and Xingtang prefect—became acting Personnel minister, Taiyuan prefect, and northern deputy regent in charge of regency.
units.literal: Yedu deputy regent and Xingtang prefect Zhang Xian was made acting Minister of Personnel, Taiyuan prefect, and northern capital deputy regent with charge of regency affairs.

units.zh: 克修，字崇遠，武皇從父弟也。
units.en: Ke Xiu, styled Chongyuan, was Li Keyong's younger cousin.
units.literal: Ke Xiu, styled Chongyuan, was the Martial Emperor's younger cousin.

units.zh: 克修少便弓馬，從父征討，所至立功，武皇節制雁門，以克修為奉誠軍使，從入關為前鋒，破黃揆於華陰，敗尚讓於梁田坡，蹙黃巢於光順門，每戰皆捷，勇懾諸軍。
units.en: Ke Xiu was skilled with bow and horse from youth. On his father's campaigns he distinguished himself wherever he fought. When Li Keyong took command of Yanmen, he appointed Ke Xiu commissioner of the Fengcheng Army. Marching into the passes as vanguard, Ke Xiu defeated Huang Kui at Huayin, routed Shang Rang at Liangtian Slope, and drove Huang Chao back at Guangshun Gate. He won every engagement, and his boldness overawed the other armies.
units.literal: Ke Xiu from youth was adept with bow and horse. Following his father on campaigns, wherever he went he achieved merit. When the Martial Emperor held military authority over Yanmen, he made Ke Xiu commissioner of the Fengcheng Army. Following him into the passes as vanguard, he defeated Huang Kui at Huayin, routed Shang Rang at Liangtian Slope, and pressed Huang Chao at Guangshun Gate. In every battle he was victorious, and his courage awed all the armies.

units.zh: 是月，平潞州，斬其刺史李殷銳，乃表克修為昭義節度使。
units.en: That month Luzhou was taken, its prefect Li Yinrui was executed, and Ke Xiu was recommended for appointment as military commissioner of Zhaoyi.
units.literal: That month they pacified Luzhou, beheaded its prefect Li Yinrui, and then memorialized to appoint Ke Xiu military commissioner of Zhaoyi.

units.zh: 克修子二人，長曰嗣弼，次曰嗣肱。
units.en: Ke Xiu had two sons: the elder, Sibi, and the younger, Sigu.
units.literal: Ke Xiu had two sons: the elder was Sibi, the younger Sigu.

units.zh: 光啟二年九月，克修出師山東，收復邢、洺。
units.en: In the ninth month of Guangqi 2, Ke Xiu took the field east of the Taihang range and recovered Xing and Ming.
units.literal: In the ninth month of the second year of Guangqi, Ke Xiu marched east of the mountains and recovered Xing and Ming.

units.zh: 文德元年十月，孟方立遣將奚忠信將兵三萬襲我遼州，克修設伏於遼之東山，大敗賊軍，擒忠信以獻。
units.en: In the tenth month of Wende 1, Meng Fangli sent Xi Zhongxin with thirty thousand men to raid Liaozhou. Ke Xiu laid an ambush on East Mountain and routed the enemy, capturing Zhongxin and sending him to headquarters.
units.literal: In the tenth month of the first year of Wende, Meng Fangli sent the general Xi Zhongxin with thirty thousand troops to raid our Liaozhou. Ke Xiu set an ambush on East Mountain of Liao and inflicted a great defeat on the rebel army, capturing Zhongxin and presenting him.

units.zh: 明年三月，卒於潞之府第，時年三十一。
units.en: and in the third month of the following year he died at the Lu prefectural residence, aged thirty-one.
units.literal: in the third month of the following year he died in the prefectural residence at Lu, aged thirty-one.

units.zh: 賊平，以功檢校刑部尚書，為左營軍使。
units.en: After the rebels were crushed, he was made acting minister of justice and commander of the Left Camp Army for his achievements.
units.literal: When the rebels were pacified, for merit he was made acting minister of justice and commander of the Left Camp Army.

units.zh: 孟方立遣將呂臻來援，戰於焦崗，大敗之，擒呂臻，俘斬萬計，進拔武安、臨洺諸屬縣，乘勝進圍邢州。
units.en: Meng Fangli sent Lü Zhen to the rescue. Ke Xiu met him at Jiaogang and won a crushing victory, capturing Lü Zhen and killing or taking prisoner tens of thousands. He then seized Wu'an, Linming, and the other subordinate counties and, riding the momentum, laid siege to Xingzhou.
units.literal: Meng Fangli sent the general Lü Zhen to relieve him. They fought at Jiaogang and inflicted a great defeat, capturing Lü Zhen. Captives and slain numbered in the tens of thousands. Advancing, they took Wu'an, Linming, and other subordinate counties, and pressing the victory moved to besiege Xingzhou.

units.zh: 莊宗即位，追贈太師。
units.en: When Emperor Zhuangzong came to the throne, Ke Xiu was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Preceptor.
units.literal: When Emperor Zhuangzong took the throne, he was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Preceptor.

units.zh: 克修性儉嗇，不事華靡，供帳饔膳，品數簡陋。
units.en: Ke Xiu was frugal by nature and shunned display. His quarters and table were spare and plain.
units.literal: Ke Xiu by nature was frugal and sparing, not given to luxury. His furnishings and meals were few and plain in kind and number.

units.zh: 武皇怒其菲薄，笞而詬之，克修慚憤發疾；
units.en: Li Keyong, angry at his austerity, had him flogged and berated him. Ke Xiu, mortified and embittered, fell ill;
units.literal: The Martial Emperor, angered at his meagerness, flogged and reviled him. Ke Xiu, ashamed and resentful, fell ill;

units.zh: 與孟方立戰於銅鞮，不利，武皇乃令克修將兵繼進。
units.en: The allied force fought Meng Fangli at Tongdi without success, so Li Keyong ordered Ke Xiu to advance with reinforcements.
units.literal: They fought Meng Fangli at Tongdi with an unfavorable outcome, and the Martial Emperor then ordered Ke Xiu to lead troops forward in succession.

units.zh: 方立求援於鎮州，王鎔出師三萬援之，克修軍退。
units.en: Fangli appealed to Zhenzhou for help. Wang Rong marched out thirty thousand men to relieve him, and Ke Xiu's army fell back.
units.literal: Fangli sought aid from Zhenzhou; Wang Rong marched out thirty thousand men to relieve him, and Ke Xiu's army withdrew.

units.zh: 及李罕之來歸，武皇授以澤州刺史，與克修合勢進攻河陽，連歲出師，以苦懷、孟。
units.en: When Li Hanzhi defected to Li Keyong, he was made prefect of Zezhou and joined Ke Xiu in a combined offensive against Heyang. Campaigning year after year, they wore down the Huai and Meng factions.
units.literal: When Li Hanzhi came over to our side, the Martial Emperor appointed him prefect of Zezhou. Together with Ke Xiu he combined forces to attack Heyang, campaigning year after year to wear down Huai and Meng.

units.zh: 大順初，潞帥李克修卒，克恭代為昭義節度使。
units.en: Early in the Dashun era, after the Lu commander Ke Xiu died, Ke Gong succeeded him as military commissioner of Zhaoyi.
units.literal: At the beginning of Dazhun, the Lu commander Ke Xiu died, and Ke Gong replaced him as military commissioner of Zhaoyi.

units.zh: 潞人素便克修之簡正，惡克恭之恣縱，又以克修非罪暴卒，人士離心。
units.en: The people of Lu had long valued Ke Xiu's plain, upright rule and resented Ke Gong's excesses. Ke Xiu's sudden death, though he was innocent of wrongdoing, also alienated the gentry and commoners.
units.literal: The people of Lu had long been accustomed to Ke Xiu's simplicity and rectitude and hated Ke Gong's wanton indulgence. Moreover, because Ke Xiu had died violently though guiltless, officials and commoners lost heart.

units.zh: 以禮部尚書王正言為戶部尚書，以御史中丞崔協為禮部尚書，以刑部侍郎、史館修撰、判館事崔居儉為御史中丞，以尚書左丞歸靄為刑部侍郎。
units.en: Wang Zhengyan, Minister of Rites, was made Minister of Revenue; Cui Xie, censor-in-chief, was made Minister of Rites; Cui Jujian, Vice Minister of Punishments, History Office compiler, and acting institute director, was made censor-in-chief; and Gui Ai, Left Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs, was made Vice Minister of Punishments.
units.literal: Minister of Rites Wang Zhengyan was made Minister of Revenue; censor-in-chief Cui Xie was made Minister of Rites; Punishments vice minister, History Office compiler, and acting institute director Cui Jujian was made censor-in-chief; Left Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs Gui Ai was made Punishments vice minister.
